# (319/100) exp(-361) is not strictly below 2^{-532}

At `p=19`, `beta0=-1/2`, bandwidth 2, and `t_i=i`, the preceding audits
show that the error of `P = p^{-20} sum_{j<J} Q^j H*` on the normalized
Schur section `0,1,2,7,8,9` is strictly below `(319/100) exp(-361)`, and
that this majorant is strictly below `2^{-513}`. The same majorant
is not strictly below `2^{-532}`.

The degree-419 Taylor sum of `exp(361)` equals
``,
which is strictly below
`1121213672233812223528563893712365791390182328701805785905578927861856397057972367681073420989954049555331851946947785581487060056017720000620090892731240054521856/25 = 2^{532} * (319/100)`.
With 420 terms, the next term is `361^420/420!` and the positive geometric
remainder envelope gives
``,
which is still strictly below that target. Every later Taylor term is
positive and inside that envelope, so

`exp(361) < 2^{532} * (319/100)`

and therefore `(319/100) exp(-361) > 2^{-532}`. No partial sum of
`exp(361)` exceeds the target. No new kappa is claimed. The selected record
is unchanged. This does not say the section error itself exceeds
`2^{-532}`; the section error remains bounded by the looser
majorant. The matrix `Q` is not formed. This is the case `C=28` for this
one majorant, not a statement about every section.

## The Taylor comparison

`FINE-PRIME.md` says the polynomial error is below `2^{-Cp}` for every
fixed `C` eventually. That claim is not decided here. Every term of the
exponential series is positive, and the degree-419 remainder envelope is
already too small to reach `2^{532} * (319/100)`.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard-library Python 3.12 or newer:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/gaussian-origin-two-power-c28/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-origin-two-power-c28
```

The verifier authenticates the pinned notes, replays the preceding
bound, and checks the remainder comparison.

## Open next questions

No larger `C` is open for this same majorant. `2^{-C p}` gets smaller
as `C` grows, and the comparison has already failed at `C=28`.
